## Confirmed findings
- [Should-fix] Final implementation contracts → Deterministic record and transition contract: “Reconstruct fetched bundles using the existing fetched_at snapshot rules to keep submit validation stable across other workers' arrivals.”; Final implementation contracts → Deterministic record and transition contract, line 108: “Reconstruct fetched bundles using the existing fetched_at snapshot rules to keep submit validation stable across other workers' arrivals.” — Stable fetched-bundle reconstruction relies on unverified fetched_at snapshot rules excluding post-fetch commits even when their timestamps equal or precede the fetch timestamp.
  verdict: confirmed (reproduce ✓ / refute ✗-survived / ground ✓)
  evidence: All three seats identify the explicit stable-submit-validation contract at spec line 108. The reused src/store/summary.rs:574–590 selects created_at<=fetched_at; fetch at 1334–1347 and insert_block at 1382–1404 both store now.0. A post-fetch commit at the same or earlier timestamp enters the reconstructed bundle. src/summary/validate.rs:166–176 then rejects B’s valid closure because A has already closed its target.
  severity: Should-fix. The demonstrated outcome is false submission rejection and rework; A’s closure still resolves the source. The seats establish no permanent data loss or failure of the core recovery purpose in this example.
  fix-shape hint: Define a persisted commit boundary or fetched membership snapshot and exercise intervening equal-timestamp and clock-rollback commits.
- [Blocking] Summary lifecycle table; Final implementation contracts / Deterministic record and transition contract — The query lifecycle specifies no honest closure path for a question that the human explicitly withdraws or replaces before it is answered.
  verdict: confirmed (reproduce REJECT / refute ✗-survived / ground ✓)
  evidence: Refute and ground cite the Summary lifecycle table: Query closes only on an answer; Request may close on cancellation; Rule may close on withdrawal or replacement. The final transition contract permits only Resolved for Query and explicitly grants cancellation only to Request. Guidance requires actual answers/completion messages. An explicitly withdrawn unanswered question therefore has no honest closure path and remains pinned as open work.
  severity: Blocking under the core-purpose floor. Refute and ground tie indefinite retention of a withdrawn obligation to the stated purpose of useful question/work lifetimes across recovery without treating human messages as permanent obligations. The reproduce dissent calls it merely unanswered; the majority directly addresses why explicit withdrawal makes that retained obligation materially wrong. This is a structural lifecycle exclusion, not the accepted uncertainty in recognizing answers.
  fix-shape hint: Permit explicit human cancellation or replacement of a Query to resolve it using a later cited withdrawal message.

## Rejected (with reason)
- [FYI] Summary lifecycle, lines 62 and 76–80; Deterministic record and transition contract, lines 106–108 — A ledger-only fallback for the chunk containing an answer, completion or rule withdrawal has no defined recovery path for the lost closure evidence.
  reason: Reproduce and refute distinguish deterministic source survival from guaranteed semantic closure. Refute cites the explicitly reused summary design §4, lines 200–207: a fallback block is final for its chunking_version as an accepted limit. The ground dissent identifies structural loss of a closure proposal, but the majority addresses that loss through the inherited final-fallback tradeoff and the absence of an eventual-closure promise. No route change.
- [FYI] Visibility across chunks; Final implementation contracts / Deterministic record and transition contract; Visibility across chunks, lines 68–72; Deterministic record and transition contract, lines 104–108 — Concurrent workers can submit independently valid closures of the same deterministic source, but final folding has no specified policy for the later closure after the first changes its status.
  reason: All three seats identify the reused still-open fold guard. Refute cites existing summary design §5: transitions whose target is no longer open are dropped and logged. Ground cites src/summary/fold.rs:49–55, 100–101, 120 and the duplicate-closure regression at 407–431. The first sequence-ordered valid closure remains; the later closure cannot reopen the source or fail the cover.
- [FYI] Summary lifecycle, lines 76–80; Deterministic record and transition contract, lines 104–106; closed-entry rendering, line 110 — The spec provides no defined repair transition for an erroneous worker-derived closure within the current summary generation.
  reason: All three seats identify an explicitly accepted semantic-judgment limit. Spec lines 72, 76 and 104 promise visibility/citation and cooperative worker judgment, not correct recognition or correction of every mistaken closure. Lines 78 and 98 preserve source messages and old-generation data. A new current-generation repair lifecycle would extend the stated contract.

## Unverified nits (spot-checked)
- [FYI] Final implementation contracts → Storage, submission and generations; Deterministic record and transition contract — The design adds a persisted withdrawn-versus-replaced distinction without defining any behavior or presentation that needs that distinction.
  verdict: unverified nit; refute spot check REJECT (FYI). One refute-seat pass does not provide panel-strength verification.
  evidence: (a) Present under another name: the distinction is specified as recorded closure evidence, not as two different lifecycle statuses. The deterministic contract requires a proposed rule_change and exact quote representing explicit withdrawal or replacement, then says to persist optional rule_change and that the final fold rechecks rule_change against canonical source kind/priority. This is a specified consumer of the persisted evidence, although neither value has a different rendering or terminal status. (b) Within the stated contract: the lifecycle table expressly assigns both explicit withdrawal and replacement the same Superseded outcome, and the final contract expressly assigns closed classified entries the existing recently-closed rendering. Equal outcomes are the chosen semantics, not a missing promised distinction. (c) Out of scope: replacement linkage or separate replacement lifecycle/presentation is not a stated goal or requirement; the design asks for active rules to survive compliance and close only on later human withdrawal/replacement. Requiring those additional features would expand that contract. (d) Immaterial: the finding identifies possible representational simplification but demonstrates no incorrect attribution, lost active rule, invalid closure, incompatible generation, or other outcome that violates the stated requirements. The small two-value evidence field has explicit submission, persistence and folding contracts; lack of separate terminal behavior alone does not establish material unnecessary complexity. The finding therefore fails refutation checks (b), (c) and (d), with a closure-evidence consumer also present under (a). Internal structural claim; no external facts are needed.
